Exercise A

Simple or continuous?

Use the past continuous for the longer action in progress and the past simple for the short action that interrupts it. Choose the correct form for each gap.

Before you start — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking. You can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Six moments from a busy week

1. While I 1 (walk) to the station, it 2 (start) to rain.

2. While we 3 (plan) our pitch, the internet 4 (stop).

3. While she 5 (check) her phone, the lecturer 6 (give) the deadline.

4. They 7 (eat) lunch at their desks when the librarian 8 (come) over and asked them to stop.

5. Our reporter 9 (present) our idea when the timekeeper 10 (hold) up the “one minute” card.

6. What 11 (you / do) when I 12 (call) you last night?

Exercise B

Finish the story

Work with your group in your breakout room. Choose one opening, plan the story together, then each person types it here. At 19:30 one group reads its story to the class.

Start with the background in the past continuous (It was raining and everyone was rushing to class…). Then tell the main events in order in the past simple (Suddenly… Then… In the end…).
